sections.history: Avur (Aavoor) lies about 12 km south-west of Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, among the Shiva shrines of the Kumbakonam country.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Pasupatheeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddesses Mangalanayaki and Pankajavalli in twin sanctums facing west, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The walled courtyard and gopuram are typical of the Shiva temples near Kumbakonam.
sections.legends: The lord is worshipped as Pasupatheeswarar, 'lord of cattle,' for the celestial cow Kamadhenu, cursed by Brahma, is said to have come here, worshipped the lord, and been freed of her curse. The twin goddesses Mangalanayaki and Pankajavalli stand in their sanctums. The fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Kumbakonam country include Avur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Avur the pilgrim comes to the lord of cattle near Kumbakonam. Before Pasupatheeswarar and the twin goddesses, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the delta, and the memory of Kamadhenu freed of her curse.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Avur lies about 12 km south-west of Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
